note: Montserrat, read on the Government of Montserrat's pages (gov.ms) on 2026-10-30: its services page for work permits and the Office of the Deputy Governor's guidance on a Permit of Permanent Residence under the Immigration (Permanent Residence Permits) Regulations 2005. The employer applies for a work permit to the Department of Labour (a self-employed form also exists); the processing fee is EC$75 for a CARICOM national and $125 for others (kept, read as Eastern Caribbean dollars, the page's other amount), before the permit's own final payment, which the page doesn't state; a renewal or variation usually takes two weeks (kept as the decision time, for a renewal); where a first permit is asked from isn't stated ('either'). A Permit of Permanent Residence may be asked by one ordinarily resident eight years immediately before applying (residence begun on or after 1 January 2003; five for residence begun before), gainfully employed the last six months, with savings averaging $5,000 or property worth $50,000, absent no more than 90 days in any year; it is applied for at the Office of the Deputy Governor and the prescribed fee isn't stated. 8 is kept as the work permit's years to it. A permanent resident may apply for naturalisation a year after the card's date; OECS citizens' freedom to work (the work engine's) isn't a residence route here.

sources.said: Click below to apply for a work permit or to renew your work permit: ... Collect renewal forms from the Department of Labour or download below for completion and signature by employer ... N.B. Processing Fee for CARICOM National=EC$75.00; OTHERS=$125.00 ... N.B. Renewal/Variation Work Permit usually takes 2 weeks to process ... Self-Employed Work Permit Form

sources.title: Government of Montserrat, Office of the Deputy Governor: Applying for a Permit of Permanent Residence under the Immigration (Permanent Residence Permit) Regulations 2005, Guidance for Applicants
sources.said: He has been ordinarily resident in Montserrat for the period of eight (8) years immediately preceding his application; ... He provides proof that he has been gainfully employed during the six (6) months immediately preceding his application for permanent residence; ... the eight (8) years immediately preceding his application he has not been absent from Montserrat in excess of days ninety (90) days ... the applicant shall pay the prescribed fee to the Accountant General

sources.title: Government of Montserrat, Citizenship & Residence Information
sources.said: Persons receiving a Permit of Permanent Residence Card or Belonger Status Card would need to wait at least a year after the date on the Card in order to apply for Naturalisation.
